findings.issue_text: Migration 20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:14 — on fresh installs with no embed_category row in site_settings, execute(...)[0] returns nil and nil['id'] raises, breaking db:migrate; the fallback query has the same problem if uncategorized_category_id is absent; needs a nil guard

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:196-201 — in the plural-id branch, hydrated || [] is dead code (map always returns an array), and if _lookupSubType returns undefined for an unknown id the resulting array contains undefined entries (the original *_ids key is deleted, so the data is unrecoverable), which will blow up when the template calls .get on them

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration 20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:29 — host values from site_settings are interpolated directly into the INSERT SQL string (VALUES ('#{h}', ...)), so a stored host containing a quote breaks the migration or allows SQL injection; use parameterized/sanitized SQL

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the loop does `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. `h` comes from `site_settings.value` (previous `embeddable_hosts` setting) and is inserted into SQL without escaping/quoting. If `h` contains a single quote it will break the SQL, and because it is raw string interpolation it also creates an SQL-injection vector (e.g., via a crafted setting value). ActiveRecord/DB quoting or parameterization should be used instead of string interpolation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:24 — params[:embeddable_host][:host] raises NoMethodError (500) if the embeddable_host param or sub-keys are missing, instead of returning a 400/validation error

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host, the code unconditionally does `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]`. If `params[:embeddable_host]` is missing (or not a Hash), `params[:embeddable_host]` will be nil and indexing `[:host]` will raise a NoMethodError, producing a 500. There is no `require(:embeddable_host)` / strong-params guard or nil-check in the diff, so a malformed request would trigger this behavior rather than returning a controlled 4xx/validation response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — the host format regex limits TLDs to 2-5 characters, rejecting valid newer gTLDs like .software and .technology

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In app/models/embeddable_host.rb the validation regex `\.[a-z]{2,5}` explicitly restricts the top-level domain to 2–5 letters. That will reject many valid modern gTLDs (e.g. `.software`, `.technology`) even though they are legitimate hostnames, making the model unable to persist such allowed hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb — no uniqueness validation on host, so duplicate host rows can be created and record_for_host silently picks an arbitrary one (first without order)

adjudication.rationale: The new EmbeddableHost model only validates host format (validates_format_of) and the migration creates embeddable_hosts without a unique index on host. Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#create allows creating new rows freely. Lookup methods record_for_host/host_allowed? use `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` without ordering, so if duplicates exist (same host differing category_id), the chosen row/category is effectively arbitrary. This can affect behavior such as TopicEmbed.import selecting `eh.try(:category_id)` based on whichever duplicate is returned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:13-15 — update is a no-op that just re-renders the embedding, and the client calls embedding.update({}) with no payload (admin-embedding.js.es6 saveChanges); the PUT endpoint and save action are dead/misleading API surface

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `update` (lines ~13-15) does not persist any changes—it just re-renders `@embedding`, and `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding` from `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`. On the client, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines `saveChanges()` which calls `this.get('embedding').update({});` with an empty payload. There is no code path in the diff that reads params or writes anything in `Admin::EmbeddingController#update`, so the PUT `/admin/customize/embedding` endpoint is effectively a no-op/misleading API surface.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:44-52 — the delete action's destroyRecord() promise has no .catch(popupAjaxError), so a failed delete silently leaves the row on screen

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... });` without any rejection handler. Unlike `save()`, which ends with `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, a failed `destroyRecord()` (e.g., network/server error) will not trigger `popupAjaxError` and will leave the UI unchanged with no explicit error feedback from this code path.

This is a verifiable lack of meaningful coverage for the added functionality.
